plays.name: Contract review and redlining
plays.sells: Cycle time to PO, not legal tooling
plays.promise: Flo reads supplier paper against your playbook, marks what changed and what the supplier left out, and sends only the deviations to a person. Clean contracts never reach legal.

glance.lead: Profile B: manufacturers on Coupa or Ariba. Also A and C.
glance.econ: VP Procurement or CPO (B), CFO (A), GC plus AI lead (C)

project: Cut contract approval time so procurement meets its SLA.
Legal or contract manager bandwidth chokes, lead times grow, and it reaches the CFO, CEO, CLO, CPO and General Counsel. That volume of complaints is why it is unavoidable.
unavoidable: AI is a board-level mandate and contract review is the chosen first use case.
Workload rose as AI clauses and complex commercials arrived.
Procurement wants to solve it without depending on legal.
Tariffs and supply chain changes force continuous contract review in manufacturing.
options: Hire procurement people with contract experience
limits: Legal is expensive to hire and train, and the G&A budget won't stretch.
Contract manager talent is scarce and expensive.
Coupa, Ariba and SAP contract modules are weak: limited OCR, manual entry, manual obligation tracking.
Review tools cut redlining time but not the approval SLA: manual handoffs remain and procurement has no CLM access.
Claude is not tied to the procurement process, not multiplayer, and can't measure outcomes.
Law firms are costly, with many handoffs and lost context.

value.headline: Make the right way to buy the easy way.
value.sub: Procurement stops being the help desk. Requesters get the right answer, what the company already owns, and a prefilled request, in the tool they already use. More spend lands on the contracts your team negotiated.
value.caveat: Outcomes are what the play is built to move, not results we have proven. In outbound, describe the shape, never a number. Structure follows your value framework: one dollar, one method, hard savings kept apart from capacity.

outcomes.name: Off-contract spend redirected
outcomes.say: "Requesters buy what we negotiated, without us chasing them."
outcomes.mech: Flo answers the request, checks the supplier master and contracts, and steers the requester to the approved catalog item or supplier before the purchase is made. The requester still submits and approvals stay in Coupa.
outcomes.hard: Spend moved from the off-contract rate to the contract rate.
outcomes.avoid: Duplicate or overlapping purchases caught before they start.
outcomes.proof: 12 months of requests, POs and invoices from Coupa, with off-contract spend by category as the baseline. Compare before and after.
outcomes.price: % of spend redirected. Internal, not for outbound. Unit price still open.

outcomes.name: Procurement capacity released
outcomes.say: "My team negotiates and sources instead of answering the same questions."
outcomes.mech: Flo answers repeat "how do I buy this" questions where requesters already ask. Procurement approves every answer in month one, then only the unusual ones.
outcomes.hard: None by default. Hours back are capacity, and become money only if procurement headcount, overtime, contractor or BPO spend moves.
outcomes.avoid: An extra hire or outside help not needed as request volume grows.
outcomes.proof: 3 to 6 months of requester questions from the help desk, Teams or email: volume, repeat share, minutes per answer. Count the intake stage only, never one blended cycle time.
outcomes.price: Per request guided. Internal, not for outbound. Unit price still open.
outcomes.cpo: My team stops answering the same ten questions.
outcomes.cfo: Request growth absorbed without adding procurement headcount.

why: A procurement assistant is a natural first AI deployment: many people use it every day. It reads as a customer support chatbot for procurement.
Requesters don't know the process and can't see where their request is. A fast, right answer is the quickest visible improvement.
A Coupa rollout earns its return when people use it. Guided buying speeds adoption without training every requester.
No PO, no pay pushes requesters into procurement's inbox. The questions arrive before the purchase, which is when guided buying helps.

Flo asks why they need it, so the right purchase is made, not just any purchase.
Flo searches the supplier master and contracts for an existing supplier or tool.
Inside the company and outside, with context on the alternatives.
Flo helps start it with fields prefilled. Anything uncertain stays with the requester. Approvals stay as they are today.

Asks in Slack, Teams or Coupa. Gets an answer, what the company already owns, and a prefilled request.
Answers the same questions all day.
Reviews exceptions. Spends the time on sourcing and negotiation.
Can't see why requesters skip the catalog.
Sees which questions and catalog gaps drive off-catalog buying.
Chases invoices that arrive without a PO.
Fewer arrive, because the request is raised before the purchase.
Spend under management stalls. The team is seen as slow.
More spend lands on negotiated contracts, and requesters get a quick answer.
lenses: Hard: off-contract spend redirected to contract pricing
Capacity: hours back, not savings until something on the P&L moves
Baseline owned by finance. Show the number at 50% of assumed adoption.
Procurement moves from answering to negotiating and strategic sourcing
People keep the judgment step. Flo prepares the answer.
Requesters learn the process by using it
Reduced: fewer non-compliant purchases and non-PO invoices
Introduced: a wrong answer, a wrong supplier or coding, chat tool data access

Month 1: recommend, with approval on every answer
Later: act with review on low-risk repeat questions. Never on approvals.

ladder.line: Make the right way to buy the easy way, inside Coupa, Slack or Teams.
ladder.spoken: Most procurement teams I talk to spend their day answering the same how-do-I-buy-this questions, and some purchases still go around the process. Flo answers requesters in Coupa, Slack or Teams, checks what you already own, and helps them start a request with the fields prefilled. The team gets time back for sourcing, and more spend lands on the contracts you negotiated.
by: Your team stops being the help desk.
Coupa stays where people buy. Flo gets them to the right item first.
Buying the right way becomes the easy way, and what you negotiated gets used.
Fewer purchases outside contract, and nobody buys what you already own.
A first AI deployment that people use every day.

project: Increase spend under management. End users want an easy way to buy.

unavoidable: AI initiatives: a customer support chatbot for procurement is a natural first deployment.
Procurement's NPS is low because end users don't know the process and have no visibility.
A new suite needs adoption to earn its multi-million investment. Guided buying speeds that ROI.
options: The suite's own help desk or guided buying

ITSM and CLM don't create the purchase request, have no supplier master, and can't set the right GL coding. Horizontal search such as Glean can't run purchase request or sourcing workflows.

Guided buying embeds in Coupa, Slack, Teams or email, with no change to the PR to PO process.

emails.subject: procurement as the help desk
emails.body: [Name], with [Company]'s [Coupa rollout / AI initiative], more requesters will be asking procurement how to buy things, and every purchase that skips your contracts works against what your team negotiated. Flo answers requesters in Coupa, Slack or Teams, steers them to what you already have on contract, and helps them start a compliant request. Worth a look at how it would handle one business unit's questions?

emails.label: Email 2: new angle, duplicate buying
emails.subject: already owned
emails.body: [Name], one more angle on requester questions: the same software gets bought twice when nobody can see what the company already owns. Flo checks your supplier master when someone asks to buy, so the first answer can be "you already have this". Does duplicate buying show up for your team, or is that handled?

emails.label: Email 3: ask for a pointer
emails.subject: who owns requester answers?
emails.body: [Name], I may be pointing at the wrong person. Who owns how requesters get answers and buy inside Coupa at [Company]? A name is plenty, and I'll stop there.

li.connect: Hi [Name], I follow how procurement teams handle requester questions around Coupa. Your work on [catalog / guided buying / procurement excellence] at [Company] caught my eye. Would be glad to connect.
li.message: Thanks for connecting, [Name]. After a Coupa rollout, I keep hearing that requesters ask procurement the same questions, and some purchases still skip the catalog. Is that close for you, or way off?

call.opener: Hi [Name], it's [Rep] from Spendflo. We haven't spoken. Can I take 30 seconds on why I called, and you tell me if it's worth another minute?
call.prop: I work with procurement leads at large companies on Coupa. They tell me their team spends the day answering the same "how do I buy this" questions, and some purchases still go around the catalog. Is that close for you, or way off?
call.close: Which questions come up most, and where do requesters ask today: email, Teams, a help desk?
call.off: Understood. What is working for you today: the catalog, a help desk, something else?

objections: We already have a help desk or ITSM.
Makes sense to use what you have. When someone asks "can I buy this", does it check your supplier master for what you already own and help them raise the request?
d
Our suite already has guided buying.
Good to use what you own. Where does it stop for a requester: does it answer and start the request, or point to the catalog?
d
Requesters won't change how they ask.
Fair. Where do they ask today: email, Teams, a ticket? The aim is to be there, not to move them.
d
We're mid-rollout. Not the time.
Understood. Is it because the catalog isn't settled, or because the team is stretched? Questions usually peak right after go-live.
d
We use an intake and orchestration tool.
Good front door for new requests. Do requesters still ask questions before they get there, and does it check what you already own?
d
Security will take months.
Usually true. Could we start the review now, in parallel, so a pilot can begin when the window opens?
w
discovery: How many requesters, and which sites or business units are on Coupa today?
Where do requesters ask for help: email, Teams, a help desk?
Which questions come up most?
What share of purchases go through the catalog, and how do you measure it?
When did duplicate software or a duplicate supplier last get bought?
Who owns catalogs, and who answers requester questions?
What would make a 30-day pilot a clear yes?
Who signs off on AI vendors, and how long does that take?
rivals: Answers but doesn't start the request. No supplier master, so no duplicate catch and no coding.
A help desk answers. Flo answers, checks what you already own, and starts the request.
A new platform. Every end user changes how they ask.
No new front door. Flo meets requesters in Coupa, Slack, Teams or email.
Can't run purchase request or sourcing workflows.
Search finds a document. Flo starts the request.
More manual touchpoints and cost. Quality drops as the team grows.
Add capacity without adding a help desk.
Not in your PULL yet. Needs research before we position against it.

can: The shape of the outcome: repeat questions answered where people ask, existing suppliers surfaced first, requests started with fields prefilled
"Uncertain fields are left to the requester"
Guided buying embeds in Coupa, Slack, Teams or email with no change to PR to PO
never: Any result number, deflection rate or NPS claim
That Flo approves spend or moves money

pilot.rule: Drafted to match the 30-day internship: read-only, one business unit, every answer reviewed by procurement before a requester sees it, a small fixed fee, no new integration.
need: Read access to Coupa catalogs, the supplier master and request history
3 to 6 months of requester questions from the help desk, Teams or email
One business unit and a named catalog owner
get: Flo drafting answers in one channel for one business unit, approved by procurement first
A ranked list of repeat questions
Duplicate or overlapping suppliers found in the supplier master
pass: Share of repeat questions answered without procurement
Share of requests started through the guided flow instead of off-catalog

landmines: No catalog owner or answer owner. Nobody to approve the answers.
A wrong answer in front of a requester. Procurement approves every answer in month one.
Slack or Teams access needs a security review. Start it in week one.
The suite's implementation partner may own catalog setup. Involve them.
An intake platform may already be chosen. Position as the layer in front, not a replacement.
Say "prefilled", not "creates the request": uncertain fields stay with the requester.
Proof gap: no reference and no numbers.
flags: No catalog or answer owner named
An intake or orchestration tool is deployed
Every signal is older than 90 days
Copy claims more than a prefilled request
